item.title: Fuuse and Drax to migrate 14,000 BP Pulse fleet charging sockets
item.dc:creator: Nicole Storch
item.description: Fuuse and Drax Electric Vehicles will support almost 1,000 fleet customers as BP Pulse exits workplace charging. The partnership aims to keep existing chargers operational, preserve hardware warranties and avoid costly replacements.

item.title: Florida campus police deploy manned eVTOLs
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: The Florida Polytechnic University Police Department is the first law enforcement agency in the USA to integrate a manned electric aircraft into its operational service. The vertical take-off aircraft is "in the final phase of the approval process," according to the university.

item.title: London Ambulance Service secures charging partners
item.dc:creator: guest author
item.description: London Ambulance Service (LAS) has contracted providers to ensure its expanding fleet of electric vehicles can be charged when and where they need power across the UK capital. SEE Services will install and maintain charging facilities and has appointed Optimo Energy as its Fleet Energy Operating System partner.

item.title: AMG Lithium opens test laboratory for solid electrolytes in Frankfurt
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: AMG Lithium has commissioned its new Performance Lab "PerLa" in Frankfurt, Germany. The company aims to test sulfide solid electrolytes under more realistic conditions in complete laboratory cells and further develop them with customers.

item.title: UK adopts EU’s Euro 7 Standard, including battery lifespan rules
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: The UK Department for Transport has confirmed that Great Britain will adopt the Euro 7 emissions standard. To minimize bureaucratic effort for automakers, there will be no separate GB-specific approval process; instead, EU and UNECE type approvals will apply so that vehicle models can be sold in parallel in both GB and the EU without additional testing.

item.title: Infineon to invest €1.1 billion in Villach
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Villach, Austria is one of the most important locations for Infineon. The market leader in chip manufacturing has now established the world's first high-volume production of GaN power semiconductors on larger 300-mm wafers at its Austrian location. Production is set to start in 2027. By 2034, around 1.1 billion euros are expected to flow into the existing infrastructure in Villach.

item.title: VW receives Level 3 test approval in China, Xpeng begins Level 4 demos
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Volkswagen Group China has been granted permission to test highly automated Level 3 driving on public roads in Hefei. Through this testing, VW aims to advance development to achieve the targeted technical maturity by 2027. Meanwhile, Xpeng has received approval for demonstration drives with Level 4 robotaxis in Guangzhou.

item.title: Polestar ends production of the Polestar 2 in China
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Production of the Polestar 2 in China is coming to an end after more than six years, where over 200,000 units of the electric fastback were built in in Luqiao. A completely new successor is set to launch in early 2027. For Polestar, the model changeover coincides with an already challenging transitional phase.

item.title: DHL acquires 25 electric swap body movers from TII Kamag
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: TII Kamag, a German manufacturer of special vehicles based in Ulm, is delivering 25 electric swap body movers to DHL. The electric vehicles are to be used in yard logistics at various DHL parcel centers across Germany. The vehicles can quickly and precisely maneuver standardised swap body containers from conventional trucks.

item.title: Volkswagen battery recall extends to Audi in the USA
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: The recall campaign for Volkswagen Group's electric cars due to potentially defective battery cells is now also expanding to Audi – especially in the USA. Around 9,000 units of the Q4 e-tron and Q4 Sportback e-tron are now being recalled in the United States. However, nearly 3,700 units are also affected in other markets.

item.title: Amazon to deploy 3,000 electric trucks in India
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: American e-commerce giant Amazon has announced plans to deploy 3,000 electric trucks in India. This will be the largest electric-truck deployment from an e-commerce company in the country.

item.title: GWM aims for European production in Bulgaria
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: At the end of 2025, Great Wall Motor (GWM) evaluated various locations for its first European plant. Indications strongly suggested that the decision would likely be Spain or Hungary. However, the Chinese automotive giant just announced at its Tech Day in Milan that its European production its vehicles – such as the Ora 5 – are set to be located in Bulgaria.

item.title: ICCT: Relaxing CO₂ standards for passenger cars threatens jobs
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: At the EU level, there are signs of a relaxation of CO₂ fleet limits for passenger cars. An ICCT study now warns that this could cost the European automotive industry up to 185,000 jobs. Notably, the auto industry itself sees jobs at risk primarily due to the strict 2035 target currently in place.

item.title: India: Ultraviolette Automotive launches its first e-2W with 100V architecture
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Indian electric two-wheeler manufacturer Ultraviolette Automotive has introduced a 100-volt electrical architecture called 'VX-100'. The Bengaluru-based startup has simultaneously launched the X-47 Venom, a crossover motorcycle, as its first application.

item.title: Thailand approves €39 million investment for Toyota Hilux FCEV production
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Thailand's Board of Investment (BoI) has approved Toyota's investment of 1.49 billion baht in its factory in Ban Pho, Chachoengsao Province, towards the production of the Hilux FCEV. BoI says this will be the first hydrogen fuel-cell electric vehicle manufactured in Thailand.

item.title: Nexeon secures £52.6m from UK National Wealth Fund
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: British battery materials developer Nexeon has secured the backing of the UK's National Wealth Fund as part of a £100 million investment round aimed at expanding its domestic operations and developing a pilot manufacturing facility. Other new investors include the Korea Development Bank and Honda Xcelerator Ventures.

item.title: Indonesia: Hyundai deploys Bali’s first electric buses for public transport
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Hyundai has handed over a fleet of eleven electric buses for public transport in Bali, Indonesia. It says these are the first e-buses that will be used for public transport in the popular tourist destination.

item.title: EVP secures majority against binding EV quotas for large corporate fleets
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: The EU Commission's draft Auto Package previously included a passage stating that member states should receive specific mandates from 2030 to accelerate the adoption of electric company cars. In the European Parliament, the proposed binding quotas are now likely to be downgraded to voluntary targets.

item.title: Qwello secures up to €55 million in growth funding
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Munich-based charging provider Qwello has secured up to €55 million from both the ABN AMRO Sustainable Impact Fund and existing shareholders to fund its further expansion. The investment will support the continued growth of Qwello's public charging network in European cities as well as targeted acquisitions.

item.title: VW could bring Chinese tech to Europe amid cost-saving pressures
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Volkswagen Group could save up to five billion euros if it adopted the China-developed CEA electronic architecture in its European volume models. However, the plan is to form a software alliance with Rivian for models outside China. This has sparked debate on the Board of Management.

item.title: Opel Agila: sister model to Citron’s electric ‘Duck’ looks likely
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: It's well-known that the Stellantis Group is planning two new entry-level electric models from 2028: the revival of Citroën's 'Duck' (2CV) and the Fiat Koala. Now, it appears there will also be a sister model from Opel, which, according to a media report, will be called the Opel Agila.

item.title: Audi adopts “two brands, two partners” strategy in China
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Audi is restructuring its joint ventures in China and will in future pursue a "two brands, two partners" approach. The joint venture with SAIC will focus exclusively on local sub-brand 'AUDI' (without rings), while the business with the four-ring vehicles will be consolidated in the joint venture with FAW.

item.title: ChargePoint launches new partner programme for distributors
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: US charging specialist ChargePoint has introduced its 'Channel Partner Program', which provides European sales companies with access to tiered pricing, growth bonuses, and marketing budgets. In return, ChargePoint expects a high level of business commitment and the completion of central training and certifications.

item.title: SVOLT launches series production of its semi-solid-state battery
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Chinese battery manufacturer SVOLT has begun series production of semi-solid-state batteries. The first batch of battery packs with 100 kWh capacity has rolled off the production line in Changzhou, Jiangsu Province. These are said to support fast charging with a charging rate of 6C.

item.title: Ionity plans battery storage systems at 50 charging parks
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Ionity has integrated a battery storage system at one of its sites for the first time, enabling the number of charging points at a charging park in Baden-Württemberg to be increased. But this is just the beginning, as Ionity now plans to install 50 battery storage systems at its charging parks next year.

item.title: Police apprehend motorised sofa in North Carolina
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: In the USA, police officers in the city of Charlotte encountered a moving sofa during nighttime traffic. The upholstered furniture was mounted on two e-scooters, with the roadworthiness of the contraption still unclear. Afterwards, the two people riding the sofa were made to continue on foot.

item.title: Plugit reports first public MCS charging session in Finland
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Charging provider Plugit has, according to its own statements, completed Finland's first public megawatt charging session. A Volvo FH Aero Electric was recharged at Plugit's MCS station in the southern Finnish port city of Kotka.

item.title: Ford adds longer-range battery and Trail version to 2027 Mustang Mach-E
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: In the US, Ford has opened order books for the 2027 Mustang Mach-E and introduced a new Trail version designed for light off-road driving. Prices start at $39,995 before delivery charges, with the larger extended-range battery now included as standard.

item.title: Stellantis moves forward with autonomous mobility initiatives in France
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Stellantis is involved in a number of new autonomous mobility initiatives in France. The group has joined a European alliance for Level 4 self-driving vehicles alongside Wayve and NVIDIA. A pilot project submitted to the ADACities programme in the Greater Paris area now aims to test autonomous driving for the first and last mile in everyday use from 2028.

item.title: Xpeng and Electronity plan more than 100 charging points in Mexico
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Xpeng is set to work with charging network Electronity to install over 100 charging points in Mexico. The partnership with the network - which is operated by Drivewatt México - initially plans to deploy 30 fast-charging points by the end of 2026. The remaining 70 charging points are set to follow by the end of 2027.
